children: The Reserve Bank of Australia has concerns about both domestic and global inflation risks, but as it is likely to raise its policy rate next week, it should also be mulling the issue of stronger local GDP growth. Westpac economist Pat Bustamante expects 3Q GDP growth at 2.3% on year, up from 2.1% in 2Q. The economy is proving more resilient than previously feared, he adds. The RBA is unlikely to be comfortable with firmer economic momentum given that it is trying to engineer a period of below-trend growth to ensure inflation returns to its target, he says. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
